policies.motor_envelope: Published continuous torque is the cap from zero to the published rated speed; zero supported torque above that speed. Known lower mechanical maximum further restricts speed. This assumes suitable FOC control and adequate stated thermal mounting, and does not invent stall torque or a mechanical speed limit.
policies.same_motor_policy: Every included motor uses the same rated_continuous envelope, including maxon variants with fuller stall data.
policies.peak_ratings: Published peaks are preserved but do not improve continuous load capacity; unknown duration remains blank.
policies.motor_mass_scope: Use source motor mass. Frameless rotor/stator sets are assumed integrated into the already modeled frame. Unmodeled custom motor housings, support bearings, encoders, wiring and controls receive no invented mass allowance; the result is a conceptual assembled-stock study rather than a complete manufactured-arm mass prediction.
policies.motor_envelope_scope: Conservative cylindrical body envelope; known complete axial lengths >=100 mm are excluded. Unknown shaft/cable envelopes remain identified in provenance.
policies.reducer_mass: Published upper-bound weights are used as conservative mass values, with their bound qualifier retained here.
policies.reducer_torque: Continuous cap is min(published rated output torque at 2000 rpm, published average output torque limit). No peak torque is treated as continuous.
policies.reducer_speed: Evaluation input speed capped at min(published mechanical maximum, average input speed limit if published, 2000 rpm). This avoids extrapolating the torque rating beyond its published reference speed.
policies.unpublished_reducer_input_torque: Remains null and is not an extra evaluated constraint. Published output torque limits and input speed limits are still enforced; input-shaft strength is not certified.
policies.reducer_inertia: Published inertia has no explicit shaft-reference declaration in the researched source, so it is not silently assigned to a rotating shaft. Rotor inertia uses published motor values.
policies.source_conflicts: Any variant with a contradictory official website/PDF field is excluded, including conflicts limited to a peak or an envelope value.
policies.availability: Only SKU-backed public-store reducer ratios are included. Procurement stock is not asserted. PDF-only and selector-only variants are not input candidates.
policies.packaging: Original approved base geometry, local assembly fit checks and derived stock masses remain authoritative. Global travel collisions and joint stops remain disabled as previously requested.
